title: Open groove cuts: a curve along a surface groove that ends on two existing rings
description:
From the review of the user's 82-ring crawfish segmentation (2026-10-04): the dorsal carapace and abdomen bands follow the cervical groove and tergite edges, but the ring tool only makes closed loops, so the user drew them as 0.7-1.2-long loops around the whole body, which then cross each other and the other rings. Wanted: an open cut, a surface curve whose two ends attach to existing rings (on the ring, sharing that point exactly), drawn with anchors like a ring and optionally following a groove (minimum principal-curvature valley) between them. The region flood treats it as a wall, so a groove cut between two rings splits the band between them. Saved in the .dsl like rings. Relates to CRAW-49 (rings sharing stretches of existing rings); the two should share the 'attach to an existing ring' mechanism.

2026-10-07: folded into the CRAW-49 rework (split a region with cuts); a cut ending on two walls is exactly this ticket's groove cut. Close this when CRAW-49 lands if its cuts cover the groove case.
definition-of-done: 1. An open cut can be drawn whose ends snap onto two existing rings. 2. The region split treats it as a wall: a band between two rings is split in two with no slivers. 3. Saved and reloaded through the .dsl. 4. Works on the crawfish carapace.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: cylinder with two rings and one open cut between them gives the expected region count. 2. Live: redraw one dorsal band of the crawfish as an open cut; screenshots.
